name: Alkem Laboratories Limited
industry: Domestic branded generics / acute therapies (anti-infectives) with a US generics and biosimilars business

moat_sources.name: intangible_assets
moat_sources.evidence_note: #1 in anti-infectives by IQVIA SSA data with 9 anti-infective brands among the IPM's top 300 (CLAVAM, TAXIM-O, TAXIM, PIPZO, MEROSURE, ZAXTER, SWICH, XONE/XONE-XP); ~4.1% overall IPM share, 5th-largest domestic formulator (9M FY25 IQVIA data, company-cited).

moat_sources.name: efficient_scale
moat_sources.evidence_note: Field force grew from >8,000 MRs / 7,000+ stockists (FY18 annual report) to >12,000 MRs / 8,000+ stockists / 70+ depots-CFAs (CARE Ratings press release, Jan 2025) -- one of India's largest branded-generics distribution footprints, a real multi-year build, not just a snapshot.

moat_sources.name: pricing_power
moat_sources.evidence_note: Domestic pricing power is structurally capped, not strong: much of the acute-therapy/anti-infective portfolio sits under NLEM/DPCO price ceilings (DPCO ceiling-price revisions covering 900+ scheduled formulations as of Apr 2025, WPI-linked increases of only 1-4%/yr historically); FY22-23 saw a real, reported margin/PAT collapse (net margin 15.8%->8.7%) when API/raw-material costs rose and could not be fully passed through. US generics (Ascend) sit in an industry-wide generic-pricing-deflation environment. This is evidence AGAINST a pricing-power moat, not for one.

moat_sources.name: cost_advantage
moat_sources.evidence_note: Scale manufacturing across a large multi-plant network gives some cost advantage, and EBITDA margin has recovered from an estimated FY23 trough to a verified 17.7% (FY24) -> 19.4% (FY25) -> 20.4% (FY26), but the FY22-23 margin collapse shows the advantage is not consistently wide or defensive versus input-cost shocks; rated HOLDING (recovering to a prior level) rather than BUILDING (a new structural low).

industry_context.phase_evidence: Alkem's core business (domestic acute-therapy/anti-infective branded generics, ~65-70% of consolidated revenue) sits in a large, well-penetrated, structurally mature segment of the Indian pharma market, which itself is forecast to grow a moderate 7.8-8.1% in 2026 (market research estimate, Tier 3). The company is expanding into chronic therapies (cardiology, diabetology, neuro/CNS) and biosimilars/CDMO (Enzene Biosciences, >Rs1,000 Cr invested) but these remain a minority of disclosed revenue -- an emergent adjacency, not yet a demonstrated segment pivot for the consolidated business.

bridge_assumptions.margin_delta_mechanism_note: EBITDA margin has verifiably expanded FY24->FY26 (17.7%->19.4%->20.4%, company results via press). A modest continuation is assumed, but DPCO/NLEM price ceilings on essential-medicine SKUs and industry-wide US-generics pricing deflation are real structural ceilings on further expansion, so the assumed delta is kept small rather than extrapolating the recent recovery trend forward.

variant_perception.market_belief: Priced as a steady, moderate-growth domestic branded-generics incumbent: trailing P/E ~27x is a meaningful discount to the Nifty Pharma index (~38-40x, itself above its own 10yr median), which the market appears to be applying because of DPCO/NLEM pricing-cap exposure, US-generics pricing pressure, and a business mix still concentrated in slower-growing acute/anti-infective therapies.
variant_perception.whats_wrong_with_belief: No confident case built either way. There IS real evidence a discount could be under-earned: 3 straight years of verified EBITDA-margin expansion (17.7%->20.4%) and IQVIA-cited share gains ahead of IPM in several core therapies in recent quarters. But there is also real evidence the discount may be fair or even insufficient: promoter holding has genuinely fallen (~56.4%->53.0% over the past year via disclosed block deals, including one promoter-group member's full exit), the Daman plant received a 7-observation USFDA Form 483 in May 2026 that is still unresolved, Q4 FY26 PAT fell 27.7% YoY on one-off charges (real-estate impairment + labour-code provision), and Q1 FY27 PAT fell 21.7% YoY on a tax-regime-switch effect -- three consecutive quarters of profit noise that make it hard to confidently separate 'temporarily depressed, mispriced' from 'the market has correctly priced a moderate-growth, margin-capped compounder.'

notes: DATA PROVENANCE: revenue and PAT for all 6 years (FY21-FY26) and EBITDA margin for FY24-FY26 are VERIFIED via web search of Alkem's own quarterly/annual results as reported by financial press (Business Standard, HDFC Sky, Indian Pharma Post, AlphaStreet, etc.) -- Tier 3 (aggregator/media reproducing company press releases), NOT Tier 1/2, because the primary sources (screener.in, careratings.com, admin.alkemlabs.com, moneycontrol) were all blocked by the egress proxy in this environment and could not be fetched directly. EBITDA margin for FY21-23 and the ENTIRE balance-sheet/cash-flow series (depreciation, debt, cash, net worth, working capital, capex, OCF, dividends for most years) are Tier 5 RECONSTRUCTED using typical Indian branded-generics capital-intensity ratios, calibrated so FY26 output matches three independently-verified ratios (ROCE ~21.2%, ROE ~18.9%, D/E ~0.09-0.17). KNOWN DISTORTION: the mechanical 3-year ROIIC/engine-growth calculation (Section 5e) uses FY23 as its base year, and FY23 was a genuine, reported margin/PAT trough (net margin fell 15.8%->8.7% on API/raw-material cost inflation post-COVID demand normalisation) -- so the recovery to FY26 will show an inflated ROIIC/engine-growth figure that overstates durable incremental capital productivity, not a genuine structural improvement. Read the engine-growth row in the Final Call Block with that in mind: the underlying business is better characterised as a ~7-9% revenue-CAGR mature compounder with margins now stabilising near 20%, not a ~30%+ engine. Market-cap band note: at ~Rs61,875 Cr the company is now well above this framework's N8 funnel screen band (Rs300-15,000 Cr) despite still trading as a Nifty Midcap 100 constituent -- index membership has lagged the company's actual market-cap growth.
